ref: Eusebius, Historia Ecclesiastica 6.20.2 (Greek numbering of Schwartz/Migne: 6.20.2; NPNF2 ch. 20 sec. 2)
greek: Ἱππόλυτος, ἑτέρας που (56) καὶ αὐτὸς προεστὼς [garbled OCR: ...] Ἐχχλησίας.
greek_edition: Migne PG 20 (1857), archive.org item patrologiae_cursus_completus_gr_vol_020, djvu OCR text (dl/pg20_djvu.txt). OCR only, Latin column interleaved; only these fragments legible; no accents verified.
english: Likewise also Hippolytus, who presided over another church somewhere, has left writings.
page: page unknown (newadvent page has no printed page numbers)
edition: Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers, Second Series vol. 1, Buffalo 1890
what_it_says: Eusebius knows a Hippolytus who was a churchman with writings but does not name his see.
use: context (identity evidence; not a Trinitarian passage)
limits: Eusebius does not say which church or city; Cerrato and Schaff read it as undecided between Rome, Portus, Arabia; Greek only in garbled OCR.

ref: Eusebius, HE 6.22.1 (NPNF2 ch. 22 sec. 1)
greek: Τότε ὅτ,τα καὶ ᾿Ἱππόλυτος συντάττων, μετὰ πλεί- στὼν ἄλλων ὑπομνημάτων, χαὶ τὸ Περὶ τοῦ Πάσχα πεποίηται σύγγραμμα (59) ἐν ᾧ τῶν χρόνων ἀνα- ἡρατὴν ἐχθέμενος, χαί τινα χανόνα ἐχχαιδεχαετηρί- ὡς περὶ τοῦ Πάσχα προθεὶς (40), ἐπὶ τὸ πρῶτον [OCR as read; ἀνα-γραφήν/ἐκκαιδεκαετηρίδος inferred from breaks, not verified]
greek_edition: Migne PG 20 (1857) djvu OCR (dl/pg20_djvu.txt). OCR errors present; accents as OCR gives them.
english: At that time Hippolytus, besides many other treatises, wrote a work on the passover. He gives in this a chronological table, and presents a certain paschal canon of sixteen years, bringing the time down to the first year of the Emperor Alexander.
what_it_says: Hippolytus wrote a Paschal work with a chronological table and a sixteen-year paschal canon down to 222 (first year of Alexander).
use: context (dating and the Paschal canon that is carved on the statue chair)
limits: Says nothing about the Trinity. The Greek is OCR only.

ref: Eusebius, HE 6.22.2 (NPNF2 ch. 22 sec. 2): list of extant works
greek_edition: Greek of 6.22.2 not legible in Migne PG 20 OCR (dl/pg20_djvu.txt); not verified.
english: Of his other writings the following have reached us: On the Hexæmeron, On the Works after the Hexæmeron, Against Marcion, On the Song of Songs, On Portions of Ezekiel, On the Passover, Against All the Heresies; and you can find many other works preserved by many.
what_it_says: Eusebius lists seven works he has read and says many more survive under other names.
use: context (the list does not include Contra Noetum or the Refutation by title)
limits: Eusebius's list has no Contra Noetum and no Refutation; Jerome's list (61) is longer and differs.

ref: Eusebius, HE 6.46.5 (NPNF2 ch. 46 sec. 5)
english: In addition to this there is extant also a certain other diaconal epistle of Dionysius, sent to those in Rome through Hippolytus.
what_it_says: Dionysius of Alexandria sent a letter to the Romans by Hippolytus's hand, so Hippolytus was a carrier of letters in Rome, not a named bishop.
use: context
limits: Only English. Does not give Hippolytus's title.

ref: Eusebius, HE 5.28.1-2 (NPNF2 ch. 28 secs. 1-2): anti-Artemon work
english: In a laborious work by one of these writers against the heresy of Artemon, which Paul of Samosata attempted to revive again in our day, there is an account appropriate to the history which we are now examining.
what_it_says: Eusebius quotes the anti-Artemon work but does not name its author.
use: context (negative result: Eusebius does not attribute the Little Labyrinth to Hippolytus)
limits: Attribution of the Little Labyrinth to Hippolytus comes from Theodoret and from scholars, not from Eusebius.

ref: Jerome, De viris illustribus 61 (NPNF2 vol. 3 numbering: ch. 61 'Hippolytus')
english: Hippolytus, bishop of some church (the name of the city I have not been able to learn) wrote A reckoning of the Paschal feast and chronological tables which he worked out up to the first year of the Emperor Alexander.
what_it_says: Jerome knows Hippolytus as a bishop of an unnamed city, with a list of works, and calls him a martyr.
use: context (identity evidence)
limits: Jerome gives no see. Latin not opened (see memory_only).
memory_only: Latin, from a search snippet quoting a commentary (not opened by me): 'Hippolytus, cujusdam Ecclesiae episcopus, nomen quippe urbis scire non potui.' UNVERIFIED. Full Latin of cap. 61 not obtained (la.wikisource index had no text).

ref: Jerome, De viris illustribus 69 (Dionysius of Alexandria)
english: Dionysius ... wrote one to Fabius, bishop of the church at Antioch, On penitence, another To the Romans, by the hand of Hippolytus, two letters To Xystus, who had succeeded Stephen ...
what_it_says: Jerome confirms the letter to the Romans was carried by Hippolytus.
use: context
limits: Only English.

ref: Photius, Bibliotheca cod. 121 (Hippolytus, 'Against the Thirty-two Heresies')
greek_edition: Greek of cod. 121 not obtained. Budé (Henry 1959-62) vol. 2 archive.org OCR shows French only; Greek not legible there. Bekker 1824 and PG 103 not reached.
english: Read the tractate of Hippolytus, the pupil of Irenaeus, entitled Against the Thirty-two Heresies. It begins with the Dositheans, and goes down to the heresies of Noëtus and the Noëtians, which he says were refuted by Irenaeus in his lectures, of which the present work is a synopsis.
page: Freese page unknown; Henry Budé French p. 95 (PDF p. 90)
edition: Freese, The Library of Photius vol. 1, London SPCK 1920. French: R. Henry, Photius Bibliothèque vol. 2, Paris Belles Lettres (1960).
what_it_says: Photius describes a 32-heresy synopsis by a pupil of Irenaeus, which goes down to Noetus. Photius's note: Hippolytus wrote on the Noetians refuted by Irenaeus.
use: context (identity: Photius calls him a pupil of Irenaeus)
limits: Scholars doubt Photius's 'pupil of Irenaeus' claim; Lightfoot notes Photius confused an anecdote about Ambrose with Hippolytus. The 'Syntagma' is lost; Refutation not named.
memory_only: PDF p. 90 is image-only (no text layer). The Hippolytus entry was OCR'd with tesseract (dl/henry_pages/ocr_90.txt): 'Lu un petit livre d'Hippolyte, Hippolyte disciple d'Irénée ... le traité combattait trente-deux hérésies.'

ref: Photius, Bibliotheca cod. 48 (marginal note on 'On the Universe'; Gaius/Josephus)
english: I find a marginal note to the effect that the work is not by Josephus, but by one Gaius, a presbyter of Rome, also the author of The Labyrinth, and of a dialogue against Proclus, the champion of the Montanists.
what_it_says: Photius's source attributes On the Universe and the Labyrinth to Gaius, a Roman presbyter, not to Hippolytus.
use: objection (authorship: Gaius rather than Hippolytus)
limits: Attribution note in a margin, not in the text. Photius cod. 48 is not the Refutation; RE (Lietzmann) says Photius names Gaius for the Refutation too.

ref: Liber Pontificalis, Pontianus (Duchesne vol. 1 text; Chronography 354 based)
greek_edition: Duchesne, Le Liber Pontificalis vol. 1, Paris 1886, archive.org duchesne01 djvu OCR (dl/duchesne1_djvu.txt, line 111489). OCR; 'deputati' appears as an apparatus variant.
translator: none (Latin only; own gloss in what_it_says)
edition: L. Duchesne, Le Liber pontificalis, t. 1, Paris 1886
what_it_says: Latin: 'Eodem tempore Pontianus episcopus et Yppolitus presbiter exilio sunt deportati ab Alexandro in Sardinia insula Bucina, Severo et Quintiano consulibus [233].' Pontian and Hippolytus both exiled to Sardinia in the consulship of Severus and Quintianus.
use: context (martyrdom and exile of 235 per LP)
limits: Date given by LP as [233] in Duchesne's bracket; Chronographer gives 235. LP text depends on the Liberian Catalogue with additions (Duchesne note 1). Hippolytus's death and reconciliation not stated here.
memory_only: page_file null: duchesne1.pdf is 159.9 MB, over the 60 MB limit, not downloaded.

ref: Depositio martyrum (Chronography 354, Calendar 'Calendriers romains', Duchesne p. 12)
edition: L. Duchesne, Le Liber pontificalis, t. 1, Paris 1886
what_it_says: Latin: 'id. aug. Ypoliti in Tiburtina et Pontiani in Calisti.' Hippolytus and Pontian share a feast on 13 August, Hippolytus buried on the Via Tiburtina.
use: context (burial and cult; Tiburtine cemetery)
limits: Calendar only; doesn't say he was a bishop. OCR.

ref: Duchesne, LP t. 1, p. 145 n. 2 (note on 'Yppolitus presbiter')
what_it_says: Own translation: 'Hippolytus, famous Roman doctor, mentioned here as Pontian's companion in exile, shares with him a common anniversary celebrated on 13 August from the time of Constantine. Duchesne argues the first part of the Liberian catalogue, down to Pontian, derives from Hippolytus's chronicle, ending at 235.'
use: scholarship (hypothesis of a lost Hippolytan chronicle behind the Liberian catalogue)
limits: Duchesne's own hypothesis, not established fact. Own translation.

ref: Liber Pontificalis, Hadrian I (Duchesne p. 511, per OCR page header)
page: p. 511 (per OCR page header; verify on scan)
what_it_says: Latin: 'simul et cymiterium beati Yppoliti martyris iuxta sanctum Laurentium' restored by Hadrian I (772-795). Hippolytus's cemetery is placed near St Lawrence.
use: context (later localization of the cult)
limits: Hadrian's restoration only; tells nothing about Hippolytus's life.

ref: Chronographer of 354, Depositio episcoporum (MGH Chron. min. I 70; Hippolytus not listed)
edition: MGH Auct. ant. IX, Chron. min. I (1892)
what_it_says: Negative: the transcribed Depositio episcoporum covers 255-352 and has no Hippolytus; the Hippolytus notice is in the 235 entry of the papal list and in the Depositio martyrum (13 August).
use: context (source map)
limits: Only a partial transcription at tertullian.org (Depositio episcoporum); Mommsen not opened.

ref: Chronography of 354, papal list entry for 235 (MGH Chron. min. I 74-75), as quoted in Lietzmann RE (1913)
greek_edition: Secondary quote in RE:Hippolytos 6 (de.wikisource); Mommsen not opened.
translator: none (Latin quoted by Lietzmann; own gloss)
page: MGH Chron. min. I pp. 74-75 (as cited by Lietzmann)
edition: MGH Chron. min. I (1892) via Lietzmann, Paulys RE VIII,2 (1913) col. 1874-1875
what_it_says: Latin as quoted: 'eo tempore Pontianus episcopus et Yppolitus presbyter exoles sunt deportati in Sardinia in insula nociva Severo et Quintiano cons.'; Pontian was stripped of office (discinctus) on 4 Oct and Anteros ordained. Own gloss: both exiled in 235.
use: context (exile and vacancy of the see in 235)
limits: Secondary quote, and differs from LP wording. Lietzmann's own reading: Hippolytus likely also gave up his office.

ref: ANF vol. 5, Introductory Notice to Hippolytus (ccel anf05.iii.ii)
english: In the year 1551, while some excavations were in progress near the ancient Church of St. Lawrence at Rome, on the Tiburtine Road, there was found an ancient statue, in marble, of a figure seated in a chair ... 'Saint Hippolytus, Bishop of Portus,' ... and states that he lived in the reign of the Emperor Alexander.
translator: unsigned ANF editorial notice (ANF vol. 5, ed. Roberts, Donaldson, Coxe)
what_it_says: The statue was found in 1551 on the Tiburtine Road. The notice reports that the Pius IV inscription calls him 'Saint Hippolytus, Bishop of Portus', and that the chair carries a Paschal table for seven 16-year cycles and a list of his works.
use: context (statue and its Portus claim)
limits: Partisan Protestant notice; accepts the Portus see. Statue's Greek inscription is not quoted here (Achelis, Hippolytstudien 3ff. per RE).

ref: Schaff, History of the Christian Church vol. 2, § 183 'Hippolytus', sec. II 'Was Hippolytus a bishop, and where?'
english: (1.) He was bishop of Portus, the seaport of Rome. ... (2.) He was bishop of the Arabian Portus Romanus, now Aden ... (3.) Rome. Hippolytus was no less than the first Anti-Pope ... History is absolutely silent about an Anti-Pope before Novatianus.
translator: Philip Schaff (own English text, HCC vol. 2, 1882)
edition: P. Schaff, History of the Christian Church vol. 2, New York 1882 (ccel hcc2.v.xv.xxv)
what_it_says: Four candidate sees: Portus, Arabian Portus Romanus, Rome (Döllinger's anti-pope view), and Salmon's independent Greek bishop; Schaff leaves it open.
use: context (three positions on the see; the anti-pope view)
limits: Secondary (1882). Schaff says the anti-pope view has no outside support.

ref: Schaff-Herzog Encyclopedia, art. 'Hippolytus' (ccel encyc05 iii.xi.lxxiii)
english: Eusebius, indeed, names eight of his works ... but is unable to give the name of his see. ... A chronographer of the year 354 (MGH, Auct. ant., ix., Chron. min., i., 1891, pp. 74-75) asserts that in 235 Pontianus the bishop and Hippolytus the presbyter were exiled to Sardinia.
translator: Schaff-Herzog encyclopedia (author not shown in the text I read)
what_it_says: Summary: Eusebius and Jerome do not give the see; the Chronographer gives the Sardinia exile; Damasus's epitaph; Prudentius's martyrdom.
use: context
limits: Encyclopedia article, secondary; says Eusebius names 'eight' works, while Eusebius lists seven. The count differs from H8-03.

ref: Cerrato, Hippolytus between East and West (OUP 2002), review in BMCR 2003.10.02
english: Nautin argued that the Refutatio, Canon paschalis, De universo and some other works are not writings of Hippolytus, but the product of certain Josephus Romanus ... On the other hand, Nautin assigns the De antichristo, the Contra Noetum and various commentaries to a non-Roman (eastern) Hippolytus.
translator: BMCR reviewer's summary (not a translation of a primary text)
what_it_says: Nautin (1948 per the review) split the corpus: Josephus Romanus for the Refutation and related works, an eastern Hippolytus for Contra Noetum.
use: objection (on whether Contra Noetum is by the Roman Hippolytus)
limits: Secondary review; date 1948 conflicts with brief's 1947. Check the title page of Nautin, Hippolyte et Josipe (Paris).

ref: Lietzmann, RE:Hippolytos 6 (Paulys RE VIII,2, 1913, col. 1873-1878)
page: col. 1874-1875 (RE columns, per the Wikisource page)
what_it_says: Own translation: 'in the same insula, Pontian was stripped of office and at the same time Hippolytus probably laid down his office; both were buried in Rome on 13 August of an unknown year.' Lietzmann dates the Refutation's last part to the Sardinian exile (after 235).
use: scholarship (dating)
limits: Own translation; secondary.

ref: Damasus, Epigram 37 (Ihm 1895 p. 42)
memory_only: Not opened. Search snippets say the epitaph calls Hippolytus a Novatianist presbyter who later returned to the Church. Latin not obtained (Ihm and Ferrua not reachable).
